title: FAR Exam Strategy & Final Comprehensive Review
description: Review high-yield FAR relationships, common traps, integrated calculations, and exam-day problem solving.
html:
You Have Reached the FAR Final Review

At this stage, the goal is no longer to memorize isolated accounting rules.

The goal is to recognize what a question is testing, identify the applicable accounting treatment, perform the calculation accurately, and follow the result through the financial statements.

FAR SUCCESS = KNOW THE RULE + IDENTIFY THE ISSUE + CALCULATE ACCURATELY + UNDERSTAND THE FINANCIAL STATEMENT EFFECT

The Universal FAR Framework

When you encounter an unfamiliar-looking transaction, break it into four questions.

1. RECOGNITION SHOULD SOMETHING BE RECORDED? 2. MEASUREMENT AT WHAT AMOUNT? 3. PRESENTATION WHERE DOES IT APPEAR? 4. DISCLOSURE WHAT ADDITIONAL INFORMATION MUST BE PROVIDED?

Recognition

First determine whether the transaction or event meets the requirements for financial statement recognition.

ASK: DOES AN ASSET EXIST? DOES A LIABILITY EXIST? HAS REVENUE BEEN EARNED? HAS AN EXPENSE OR LOSS BEEN INCURRED?

Measurement

Once an item should be recognized, determine the appropriate measurement basis.

POSSIBLE MEASUREMENT CONCEPTS: HISTORICAL COST AMORTIZED COST FAIR VALUE NET REALIZABLE VALUE PRESENT VALUE ESTIMATED AMOUNT

Do not choose a measurement basis simply because it appears reasonable. Apply the accounting rule for the specific item.

Presentation

FAR frequently tests where an amount belongs, not merely how much it is.

CURRENT OR NONCURRENT? NET INCOME OR OCI? ASSET OR CONTRA-ASSET? LIABILITY OR EQUITY?

Disclosure

Some matters may require disclosure even when no amount is recognized.

NO JOURNAL ENTRY DOES NOT ALWAYS MEAN NO FINANCIAL REPORTING CONSEQUENCE

Loss contingencies and certain subsequent events are common examples.

Master the Accounting Equation

ASSETS = LIABILITIES + EQUITY

When you are unsure about an adjustment, trace its effect through this equation.

Income Statement Connection

REVENUE ↑ → NET INCOME ↑ → EQUITY ↑ EXPENSE ↑ → NET INCOME ↓ → EQUITY ↓

This relationship can help you solve questions even when the journal entry is not immediately obvious.

Accrual Accounting

Never assume that revenue equals cash received or expense equals cash paid.

RECOGNITION ≠ CASH MOVEMENT

Accrued Revenue

REVENUE EARNED BEFORE CASH RECEIVED → ASSET ↑ REVENUE ↑

Accrued Expense

EXPENSE INCURRED BEFORE CASH PAID → LIABILITY ↑ EXPENSE ↑

Deferred Revenue

CASH RECEIVED BEFORE PERFORMANCE → LIABILITY PERFORMANCE SATISFIED → LIABILITY ↓ REVENUE ↑

Prepaid Expense

CASH PAID BEFORE BENEFIT CONSUMED → ASSET BENEFIT CONSUMED → ASSET ↓ EXPENSE ↑

Inventory Formula

BEGINNING INVENTORY + PURCHASES − ENDING INVENTORY = COST OF GOODS SOLD

Memorize the relationship rather than memorizing individual error rules.

Inventory Error Logic

ENDING INVENTORY ↑ → COGS ↓ → NET INCOME ↑ ENDING INVENTORY ↓ → COGS ↑ → NET INCOME ↓

Receivables

NET ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE = GROSS ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE − ALLOWANCE FOR CREDIT LOSSES

Long-Lived Assets

CARRYING AMOUNT = COST − ACCUMULATED DEPRECIATION − APPLICABLE IMPAIRMENT

Straight-Line Depreciation

ANNUAL DEPRECIATION = COST − RESIDUAL VALUE ÷ USEFUL LIFE

Held-and-Used Asset Impairment

STEP 1: CARRYING AMOUNT VS UNDISCOUNTED EXPECTED FUTURE CASH FLOWS STEP 2: IF NOT RECOVERABLE → LOSS GENERALLY BASED ON CARRYING AMOUNT MINUS FAIR VALUE

Bonds

INTEREST EXPENSE = BEGINNING CARRYING AMOUNT × EFFECTIVE RATE CASH INTEREST = FACE VALUE × STATED RATE

Bond Direction Shortcut

DISCOUNT → CARRYING AMOUNT INCREASES TOWARD PAR PREMIUM → CARRYING AMOUNT DECREASES TOWARD PAR

Contingencies

PROBABLE + REASONABLY ESTIMABLE → ACCRUE REASONABLY POSSIBLE → GENERALLY DISCLOSE REMOTE → GENERALLY NEITHER

Accounting Changes

PRINCIPLE → GENERALLY RETROSPECTIVE ESTIMATE → PROSPECTIVE ERROR → CORRECT PRIOR PERIODS

Subsequent Events

CONDITION EXISTED AT YEAR-END? → GENERALLY ADJUST CONDITION AROSE AFTER YEAR-END? → GENERALLY DO NOT ADJUST BUT MATERIAL DISCLOSURE MAY BE REQUIRED

Investments

TRADING DEBT SECURITY → FAIR VALUE CHANGES IN NET INCOME AVAILABLE-FOR-SALE DEBT SECURITY → UNREALIZED HOLDING GAINS / LOSSES GENERALLY IN OCI HELD-TO-MATURITY → AMORTIZED COST

Equity Method

SHARE OF INVESTEE INCOME → INVESTMENT ↑ DIVIDENDS RECEIVED → INVESTMENT ↓

Statement of Cash Flows

Separate the accounting effect from the cash-flow classification.

OPERATING INVESTING FINANCING

Indirect Method Pattern

OPERATING ASSET ↑ → SUBTRACT OPERATING ASSET ↓ → ADD OPERATING LIABILITY ↑ → ADD OPERATING LIABILITY ↓ → SUBTRACT

Governmental Accounting Shortcut

Before doing anything else, identify which reporting level is being tested.

GOVERNMENTAL FUND → CURRENT FINANCIAL RESOURCES + MODIFIED ACCRUAL GOVERNMENT-WIDE → ECONOMIC RESOURCES + ACCRUAL

Governmental Capital Assets and Debt

GOVERNMENTAL FUND: CAPITAL OUTLAY → EXPENDITURE GENERAL LONG-TERM BOND PROCEEDS → OTHER FINANCING SOURCE
GOVERNMENT-WIDE: CAPITAL ASSET → CAPITALIZE LONG-TERM DEBT → LIABILITY

NFP Shortcut

FIRST: CONDITION? THEN: DONOR RESTRICTION? THEN: HAS RESTRICTION BEEN SATISFIED?

NFP Conditions vs Restrictions

CONDITION → AFFECTS WHETHER CONTRIBUTION IS RECOGNIZED RESTRICTION → AFFECTS HOW RECOGNIZED NET ASSETS ARE CLASSIFIED

Do Not Memorize Without Understanding

Formulas are useful, but FAR questions can change the facts.

Understanding why the formula works is more reliable than memorizing a mechanical answer pattern.

MCQ Strategy

READ THE REQUIREMENT ↓ IDENTIFY THE TOPIC ↓ WRITE THE RULE / FORMULA ↓ USE ONLY RELEVANT FACTS ↓ CALCULATE ↓ CHECK WHETHER THE ANSWER MAKES ACCOUNTING SENSE

Watch for Distractors

CPA-style questions may provide information that is not needed for the required calculation.

MORE NUMBERS ≠ USE EVERY NUMBER

Read the Requirement Carefully

A question may ask for:

REVENUE NOT CASH CARRYING AMOUNT NOT FAIR VALUE EXPENSE NOT CASH PAYMENT CURRENT LIABILITY NOT TOTAL LIABILITY FUND-LEVEL AMOUNT NOT GOVERNMENT-WIDE AMOUNT

Answer the exact question being asked.

TBS Strategy

Task-based simulations can contain much more information than MCQs.

Break the simulation into smaller independent requirements.

1. READ THE REQUIREMENT 2. IDENTIFY THE RELEVANT EXHIBIT 3. SOLVE ONE CELL OR REQUIREMENT AT A TIME 4. CHECK SIGNS AND CLASSIFICATIONS 5. RECONCILE TOTALS 6. REVIEW BEFORE SUBMITTING

Do Not Let One TBS Destroy Your Time

If one requirement is difficult, continue solving the portions you can determine independently.

ONE DIFFICULT CELL ≠ ENTIRE TBS LOST

Use Reasonableness Checks

Before accepting an answer, ask whether its direction makes sense.

EXAMPLE: BOND DISCOUNT AMORTIZATION SHOULD MOVE CARRYING AMOUNT TOWARD FACE VALUE

If your calculation moves it farther away, recheck your work.

Integrated Final Example

A company reports preliminary net income of $500,000.

The following adjustments remain:

Accrued salaries: $30,000

Accrued revenue: $20,000

Depreciation: $40,000

Probable and estimable lawsuit loss: $15,000

Ending inventory is understated: $10,000

Solve Each Adjustment Separately

SALARIES − $30,000 ACCRUED REVENUE + $20,000 DEPRECIATION − $40,000 LAWSUIT − $15,000 INVENTORY UNDERSTATEMENT → COGS OVERSTATED → CORRECTING IT + $10,000 TO INCOME

Corrected Net Income

$500,000 − $30,000 + $20,000 − $40,000 − $15,000 + $10,000 = $445,000

Final FAR Checklist

BEFORE FINALIZING AN ANSWER: ✓ CORRECT ACCOUNTING RULE? ✓ CORRECT PERIOD? ✓ CORRECT MEASUREMENT? ✓ CORRECT CLASSIFICATION? ✓ CORRECT SIGN? ✓ CORRECT FINANCIAL STATEMENT EFFECT? ✓ ANSWERED WHAT WAS ACTUALLY ASKED?

What Mastery Looks Like

FAR mastery does not mean that every question looks familiar.

It means that when a new scenario appears, you can break it into accounting concepts you understand and work toward the answer.

DON'T ASK: "HAVE I SEEN THIS EXACT QUESTION?" ASK: "WHAT ACCOUNTING CONCEPT IS THIS TESTING?"

Final Takeaways

  • Start with recognition, measurement, presentation, and disclosure.
  • Trace transactions through the accounting equation and net income.
  • Keep accrual accounting separate from cash movement.
  • Understand relationships instead of memorizing isolated answers.
  • For governmental questions, identify fund-level versus government-wide reporting first.
  • For NFP contributions, separate conditions from donor restrictions.
  • For cash flows, separate the income statement effect from the cash classification.
  • Break large TBSs into individual requirements.
  • Use reasonableness checks before finalizing calculations.
  • Always answer the exact requirement presented by the question.

quiz.prompt: A company reports preliminary net income of $500,000. It has unrecorded accrued salaries of $30,000, accrued revenue of $20,000, depreciation of $40,000, a probable and reasonably estimable lawsuit loss of $15,000, and ending inventory is understated by $10,000. What is corrected net income?
quiz.explanation: Corrected net income is $500,000 − $30,000 + $20,000 − $40,000 − $15,000 + $10,000 = $445,000. The inventory understatement caused COGS to be overstated, so correcting the inventory error increases income by $10,000.
